## How to schedule a text message on iPhone and Android


Need to send a text later but don't want to forget? Both iPhone and Android users can schedule text messages, but the methods vary by device. Below, we'll walk you through how to schedule a text message, from native options to workarounds (that actually work).


Let’s explore options for scheduling text messages on both iPhone and Android.


## Can you schedule a text on iPhone or Android?


Yes, you can[schedule a text message](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/schedule-a-message-in-twilio-studio) natively on both iPhone and Android without downloading any third-party apps. On iPhone (iOS 18 or later), open the Messages app, tap the + icon, select Send Later, and pick your date and time. On Android (Google Messages), type your text, press and hold the Send button, and choose a scheduled send time.


And if you’re interested in sending scheduled messages to your customers at scale, we include a section below that explains how to automate SMS scheduling using Twilio.

## How to schedule a text on iPhone


Can you schedule a text on iPhone? Yes, now you can! Thanks to a recent update, you can now schedule a text message directly from iMessage. Here's how to do it (along with the old workarounds, too, if you prefer):


### Option 1: Use the Native Scheduler in iMessage (iOS 18+)


Apple added built-in text scheduling to iMessage, and this is now the easiest and most reliable way to schedule texts on iPhone. You'll need iOS 18+ to access it:


**Step 1:** Open Messages. Go to an existing conversation or start a new one.


**Step 2:** Tap the "+" icon next to the text field. Select "Send Later" from the menu.


**Step 3:** Tap the time field to open the scheduler. Select when you want to send your message (up to 14 days ahead). The text field border will turn into a dashed line


**Step 4:** Type your message. Tap the send arrow to schedule it. Your message appears with a dashed border until it sends.


Here's a couple things you need to know about scheduling text messages with iPhone's native function:


-


**Works offline:** Messages send even if your phone is turned off (yeah, that's pretty cool) because they are queued on Apple's servers


-


**Edit/reschedule:** Touch and hold scheduled messages to edit the text, change the send time, or cancel it.


-


**Encrypted:** Scheduled messages are securely stored on Apple servers until delivery.


-


**No indication to recipient:** They won't know the message was scheduled.


### Option 2: Use a Shortcuts automation (best for SMS to Android or iOS 17 and earlier)


The[Shortcuts](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/shortcuts/id915249334) app allows you to create automations, including sending scheduled text messages to Android users or on older iPhones. This option requires some maneuvering, but it’s free and comes preinstalled on devices running iOS 13 or later. This method sets up a recurring message. Later, we’ll cover how to remove the automation when you want to cancel it after a one-time send.


-


**Step 1:** Open the Shortcuts app. If you can't find the app on your home screen, swipe down and enter “Shortcuts” in the search bar.


-


**Step 2:** Tap the Automations tab at the bottom of the screen. Tap Create Personal Automation (or tap the + sign in the upper-right corner if you already have existing automations).


-


**Step 3:** Create your automation. Select the Time of Day automation. Then, set the time when you want to send your message. Next, in the Repeat section, select Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. For a one-time message, select Monthly, choose the date, and tap Next.


-


**Step 4:** Compose your message. Tap Add Action, then select Send Message. Type your text in the Message field and choose the recipient. Then, tap Next.


-


**Step 5:** Review and finalize the automation. Check the date, time, recipient, and message to ensure everything is correct.Toggle off Ask Before Running if you want the automation to run automatically without requiring confirmation. Finally, tap Done.


-


**Step 6:** Set a reminder to delete the automation. If you only need to send a one-time message, open the Shortcuts app after it sends, navigate to the message automation, swipe left, and tap Delete. This will remove the automation.


### Option 3: Use a third-party app


The App Store has plenty of third-party applications—like[Scheduled](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/scheduled-a-reminder-for-your-messenger/id1145815975) or[Text Delay](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/later-schedule-texts-email/id725222144) —that you can use to schedule a text message. Some apps are free, and others will require a fee to access advanced features. A few options don’t actually send the text message you’ve scheduled—instead, you’ll get a notification to send the message yourself at the scheduled time.


### Option 4: Use the iPhone Reminders app


If you’d rather not download anything new, consider using your iPhone’s preinstalled[Reminders app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/reminders/id1108187841) as a workaround. The Reminders app won’t send your text message at a desired time, but it'll give you the option of composing your message in advance. Then, you can set a reminder to prompt you to manually send the message when desired.


**Step 1:** Open the Reminders app. Pull down on the home screen and enter “Reminders” in the search bar if the app isn’t visible on the home screen.


**Step 2:** Add a list. Tap on Add List in the lower-right corner. (Or to add the reminder to an existing list, tap on + New Reminder in the lower-left corner, title the reminder, and go to Step 5.)


**Step 3:** Enter your details. Title your list (such as "text messages") and choose a color.


**Step 4:** Add a reminder. Tap on + New Reminder in the lower-left corner and title your reminder (such as "text Zach").


**Step 5:** Choose a time and date to send, and compose your text. Tap the details icon to the right of the label (the “i” enclosed in a circle) to include a date and time to receive your notification. If you’d like to create your text so that you don’t have to do it later, enter it in the Notes section. Tap Done. Or if you just want a general reminder to send a text, tap on the calendar icon that appears above the keyboard (it features a clock icon) and choose to send the reminder to yourself today, tomorrow, or over the weekend.


**Step 6:** Copy and paste the text into iMessage when you get your reminder. Open your reminder when it pops up at the scheduled time and follow these steps:


-


Open the reminder details.


-


Double tap the note—a highlight will appear.


-


Drag the highlight to select the entire message.


-


Tap Share.


-


Choose your recipient from the pop-up options and paste the selected text into the blank field. Alternatively, tap on the messages icon, add your recipient, and double tap to paste the selected text into the blank field.


## How to schedule a text on Android


So far, this guide has explained how to schedule texts on iPhone, but Android users may be asking, can you schedule a text on Android? The answer is yes. Android users have a few options to send a scheduled text message. Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel device owners have the fewest steps, while others will need to use a work-around method or download a third-party app. Here's how to send a delayed text on Android using four different methods.


### Option 1: Use the Messages by Google app (Google Pixel, Motorola, and Modern Samsung Galaxy)


Messages by Google is the default texting app on most modern Android devices—including Google Pixel and newer Samsung Galaxy phones—and includes native text scheduling. If not preinstalled on your device, you can download Messages by Google for free from Google Play and set it as your default texting app.


-


**Step 1:** Open the Messages by Google app.


-


**Step 2:** Compose the message. Select an existing text conversation or tap Start chat to begin a new one, then select the recipient and type your message.


-


**Step 3:** Schedule the message. Tap and hold (long-press) the Send arrow until the Schedule send menu appears. Choose from the suggested send times or select Pick date and time to manually select when you want to send your message.


-


**Step 4:** Finalize the send. Confirm that the date and time in the preview window are correct, then tap Save. Finally, tap Send to schedule your message.


### Option 2: Use the Samsung Galaxy Messages app (older Galaxy devices)


If you have a Samsung Galaxy phone using the legacy Samsung Messages app, you can schedule a text message directly inside the chat.


-


**Step 1;** Open Samsung Messages.


-


**Step 2:** Compose your message. Tap Compose in the lower-right corner, then select your recipient and write your text.


-


**Step 3:** Schedule the message. Tap + or the arrow on the left side of the text field.


-


**Step 4:** Set a time and date. Tap the Schedule message icon and enter a date and time up to a year from the current date.


### Option 3: Use your Google Calendar app


This option is a workaround to schedule a text message that serves more as a reminder with the option to write the text ahead of time. The steps below are for[Google Calendar](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.google.android.calendar) since it’s the default calendar app on every Android phone, but other calendar apps offer similar functionality.


-


**Step 1:** Open the Calendar app. Swipe up on the home screen and enter “Calendar” in the search bar to access the app.


-


**Step 2.:** Create a new event. Tap + (Create), then tap Event.


-


**Step 3:** Choose a date and time to send and compose your text. Swipe up to edit the event details. Add a title (such as "text mom"), include the date and time you’d like to send the text, and enter your text message in the Notes section. Then, set the time for a notification reminder. You may want to set the notification to a minute before the event so that it’s as close as possible to the time you want to send it.


-


**Step 4:** Receive your reminder, then copy and paste the text to your recipient. Open the event when you get your reminder notification and follow these steps:


-


Open the event notes.


-


Select the text and copy it.


-


Open your default text message app.


-


Choose your recipient and paste the selected text into the text field.


### Option 4: Use a third-party app


If you’re open to downloading an app, you can use a third-party messaging app that comes with a scheduling feature. A few popular, well-reviewed apps are[Pulse SMS](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=xyz.klinker.messenger&hl=en_AU) and[Textra SMS](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.textra&hl=en_AU) . Keep in mind that some apps display advertisements, and others will require a fee to access advanced features.


## When to schedule a text message to customers


Using texting software to[send automated text messages](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/how-to-send-automated-text-messages) is a time saver and can be helpful in the following scenarios:


-


**Marketing campaigns:** Preplanning is a must when it comes to marketing campaigns. Schedule timely messages to let customers know about upcoming sales or special events.


-


**Deadline alerts:** Sometimes customers need a little nudge. Prompt them to remember registration deadlines, sign digital documents, and more.


-


**[Appointment reminders](https://www.twilio.com/blog/appointment-reminder-texts) :** Missed appointments waste time and hurt revenue. By scheduling a reminder the moment you set the appointment, you'll spare yourself the need to remember to do it as the appointment approaches.


-


**Billing date reminders:** Some customers prefer a notification when you charge their credit card or when they need to make a payment. A text message ensures they’ll see the message right away.


-


**Follow-up with prospects:** Building a relationship with prospects is an essential sales strategy. Stay in touch by scheduling a few follow-up texts throughout the sales cycle.

## Text scheduling FAQs


### Can you use a personal phone to schedule business texts?


Yes, you can send business texts from a personal phone, but you'll have to take precautions to avoid business, legal, and security complications. Your personal phone may lack business functionality and security features, and using your personal number may make you vulnerable to spam complaints and cybersecurity risks.


Fortunately, utilizing your personal phone doesn't mandate sending texts from your personal phone number. Instead, you can install an app to send messages from a business phone number. A business app provides enterprise-level messaging functionality with features dedicated to team collaboration, marketing, and security. Before sending messages, remember to obtain recipient consent to avoid violating spam regulations.


### Can you tell if a text was scheduled?


Senders can tell if texts are scheduled, but recipients generally can't. However, app developers can build scheduling information into texts if desired.


### How do scheduled text messages work?


Scheduled messages include a code instructing your messaging service when to send your message. Your messaging provider may require that your message be sent within a specified time frame. For instance, Twilio's Message Scheduling feature currently allows[scheduled SMS](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/send-scheduled-sms-node-js-twilio) messages to be sent anywhere from 15 minutes to 35 days in the future.


### What kinds of texts can you schedule?


You can schedule messages for a variety of purposes, including marketing and sales communications and customer support reminders. Marketing and sales messages can be used to announce upcoming sales or follow up with prospects, while customer support messages can serve to remind customers of appointments or deadlines.


### When is the best time to schedule a text?


The best time to schedule a text depends on the purpose of your text as well as your recipient's schedule. Send reminder texts sufficiently in advance of event deadlines, typically at least 24 hours ahead of time. B2B marketing messages are best sent during business hours, at times when recipients are most likely to check their messages, such as early morning, lunch hour, and the end of the business day. B2C recipients tend to check their phones more frequently outside of business hours. These general guidelines vary by market, so for best results, track your own recipient list's text viewing patterns.


### How do I edit or cancel a scheduled text message?


On iPhone (iOS 18+), open the Messages thread, tap Edit above the dashed message bubble, and choose Edit Time or Delete Message. On Android (Google Messages), tap the clock icon next to the scheduled message in the conversation to edit the text, change the send time, send it immediately, or delete it.


### Can you schedule a text message on iPhone to an Android user?


Not natively using iMessage's Send Later feature, which currently only works for blue-bubble iMessage chats between Apple devices. To schedule a text to an Android user from an iPhone, you must either set up a Time of Day automation in the Apple Shortcuts app or use a third-party reminder app.
